title: Beautiful Towers I
summary: Given an array of tower heights, rearrange the towers to form a mountain shape with the highest possible total height.
statement: Given an array of tower heights, rearrange the towers to form a mountain shape with the highest possible total height. The mountain shape must rise to a peak and then fall, with the peak being one or more consecutive towers.
constraints: heights is a nonempty array of positive upper bounds.
Choose positive heights no greater than their bounds that are nondecreasing to a peak and nonincreasing afterward.
Return the maximum possible total chosen height.
hints: Fixing a peak determines the greatest feasible heights outward by repeated minima.
Use monotonic stacks to compute the optimal constrained prefix and suffix sum for every possible peak.
For each peak combine left_sum+right_sum-peak_height and take the maximum.
The nearest lower bound found by each stack compresses the repeated-minimum runs, producing exactly the same mountain as outward clamping for every peak.
editorial: The nearest lower bound found by each stack compresses the repeated-minimum runs, producing exactly the same mountain as outward clamping for every peak.

tests.explanation: Choosing [5,3,3,1,1] with its peak at index zero totals thirteen.
